name: Latundê
catalog_citation: Telles, Stella. 2012. Vogais nasais em Latundê (Nambikwára do Norte). Letras de Hoje (Porto Alegre, PUCRS) 47(3): 293-298. [open-access journal PDF, CC BY-NC-ND 3.0]
catalog_locator: p.293, section 1 'Introdução' ( continuing at the top of column 2, two-column layout); examples p.295 (txt, 198-199)
catalog_quote: Em nível prosódico, o correlato fonético do acento é o tom (pitch), constituindo um sistema prosódico conhecido na literatura como pitch accent. O acento é lexical e a ele se combina o acento métrico, sensível ao peso silábico. Além disso, há um tom de nível que opera em processos morfofonológicos. ... Os domínios fonológicos relevantes são a sílaba, o morfema e a palavra fonológica. [p.295, underlying forms mark lexical accent per morpheme:] [ˈawmˌde] /ˈawn-ˈte/ ‘louro’ ... [ˌa̰:ˈnde] /a̰n-ˈte/ ‘maribondo’ ... [ˈna̰:ˌde] /ˈna̰n-ˈte/ ‘sangue’ ... [ˈnã̰:ˌde] /ˈnã̰n-ˈte/ ‘folha’ e [ˈna̰:ˌde] /ˈna̰n-ˈte/ ‘sangue’. [Abstract, p.293:] A ocorrência dessas vogais é restrita à posição do acento, uma vez que em silaba átona o contrate nasal é neutralizado.

new_statements.quote: Em nível segmental, no Latundê se observam vinte e sete fonemas, dos quais onze são consoantes e dezesseis são vogais. Em nível prosódico, o correlato fonético do acento é o tom (pitch), constituindo um sistema prosódico conhecido na literatura como pitch accent. O acento é lexical e a ele se combina o acento métrico, sensível ao peso silábico. Além disso, há um tom de nível que opera em processos morfofonológicos.
new_statements.translation: At the segmental level Latundê has twenty-seven phonemes, eleven consonants and sixteen vowels. At the prosodic level, the phonetic correlate of stress is pitch, constituting a prosodic system known in the literature as pitch accent. Stress is lexical, and combined with it there is a metrical stress that is sensitive to syllable weight. In addition, there is a level tone that operates in morphophonological processes.
new_statements.citation: Telles, Stella. 2012. Vogais nasais em Latundê (Nambikwára do Norte). Letras de Hoje (Porto Alegre, PUCRS) 47(3): 293-298.
new_statements.locator: p.293, section 1 'Introdução' (the text layerof extracted text page 1)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (Telles 2012, Letras de Hoje 47(3), CC-licensed open access via CORE/PUCRS OJS) opened; extracted text of p.1 (=journal p.293, section 1 'Introducao') contains the quoted passage word for word: 'Em nivel segmental, no Latunde se observam vinte e sete fonemas.. Em nivel prosodico, o correlato fonetico do acento e o tom (pitch), constituindo um sistema prosodico conhecido na literatura como pitch accent. O acento e lexical e a ele se combina o acento metrico, sensivel ao peso silabico. Alem disso, ha um tom de nivel que opera em processos morfofonologicos.' The only artefact is the two-column layout (the sentence breaks at 'O acento e | lexical' across the column/footer), no wording diff…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per the primary describer (Telles), Latundê accent is lexical (certain roots and affixes carry inherent accent, marked in her underlying forms, e.g. /ˈna̰n-ˈte/ -> [ˈna̰:ˌde] 'blood' vs unaccented root /a̰n-ˈte/ -> [ˌa̰:ˈnde] 'wasp'), supplemented by a weight-sensitive metrical default. The detailed default (Telles 2002 as summarised second-hand by Costa 2020: 307-308, 312-313): domain is the root (and word); in disyllabic roots the heavy syllable is stressed, if both are light the rightmost is stressed and its vowel lengthened; in trisyllabic roots the final syllable if heavy, otherwise a heavy first syllable takes primary and the last secondary; coda consonants (incl. nasals) are moraic (Telles 2019: 174). Pitch (H on stressed, L on unstressed) and duration are the correlates; later work (Telles 2013; Braga & Telles 2014) reanalyses the system as mixed stress + two-level lexical tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Costa 2020 (second-hand from Telles 2002): when a word has several (lexical) stresses the leftmost is primary and the others secondary; in roots with two heavy syllables one takes primary and the other a phonetic secondary stress; grammatical suffixes such as referential -te, imperfective -tãn surface with (secondary or primary) stress. Telles's own transcriptions (2012, 2013) mark ˈ and ˌ accordingly.
new_statements.exceptions: Lexically accented vs unaccented roots are distinguished by relative prominence (Costa 2020 Quadro 71); Telles 2013: 294 and Braga & Telles 2014: 64 state the 2002 pitch accent analysis is being revised to a mixed stress+tone system (contrastive H not always tied to stress).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns word-level prosody of (polysynthetic) morphological words; Costa 2020 reports Telles's stress domain as root and word; Telles 2012 fn.1 defines the phonological word as the domain of the relevant rules. Examples are citation forms of inflected words.
new_statements.identity_note: All Telles sources describe Latundê proper (latu1238, T.I. Tubarão-Latundê, Rondônia; <25 speakers, fieldwork 1997-2001). Her 2002 thesis and the Costa 2020 summary treat Latundê and Lakondê (lako1248) jointly as one phonological system ('Latundê/Lakondê'); the quoted 2012 statement is about Latundê alone. Braga 2012 concerns Lakondê only.
